claims.text: Homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi initially has a dual-phase FCC/B2 lamellar structure.
The initial FCC/B2 interfaces are incoherent and create stress concentrations that cause brittleness.
The proposed treatment uses a hexahedron-anvil apparatus at approximately 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours.
Treatment at 6 GPa and 1473 K will transform the incoherent FCC/B2 lamellae into a hierarchically patterned microstructure with coherent interfaces.
A temperature of 1473 K is sufficient for the diffusion and rearrangement needed for the proposed topological transformation.
The proposed pressure and temperature remain below the phase-instability or lamellar-degradation limit under HPHT conditions.
The pressure-assisted transformation replaces incoherent FCC/B2 boundaries with coherent FCC/B2 interfaces.
Coherent FCC/B2 interfaces facilitate dislocation transfer between the two phases.
Interphase dislocation transfer alleviates stress concentrations that would otherwise cause interfacial cracking.
The transformed structure activates dislocation transfer, stacking faults, and twinning as concurrent deformation mechanisms.
These deformation mechanisms produce a more homogeneous strain distribution and arrest crack propagation.
After HPHT treatment, GND densities in the FCC and B2 phases will converge at high strain.
The HPHT-treated material will exhibit elongated crack paths rather than isolated microcracks.
HPHT treatment will simultaneously enhance yield strength and ductility relative to the baseline.
The DPHL700 and DPHL740 samples produced by conventional thermomechanical processing exhibit hierarchical FCC/B2 heterogeneity and simultaneous strength–ductility improvement.
Annealing at 900 °C degrades the lamellar structure in the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 material.
Very low interphase lattice mismatch can be achieved through other processing routes.

The hypothesis is falsified if HPHT does not create coherent interfaces, does not cause FCC and B2 GND densities to converge, or does not simultaneously improve strength and ductility relative to the controls.
